proposal.reactor_type: 5 mL SS packed-bed reactor charged with Pd(OH)2/Al2O3 catalyst specified in the batch protocol
proposal.residence_time_basis: Nominal liquid residence time based on the full stated 5.0 mL reactor volume divided by the 0.100 mL/min liquid feed rate. This is a screening target, not a measured catalyst-bed void-volume residence time; actual liquid hold-up will be lower if the listed 5 mL is total reactor volume rather than interstitial bed volume.
proposal.light_setup: No light source; thermal hydrogenolysis only.
proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Meter the methanolic substrate solution and hydrogen separately into the certified gas-liquid mixer immediately upstream of the heated packed bed. This minimizes uncontacted hydrogenated liquid volume while providing a defined hydrogen excess before the catalyst bed. At 1.0 sccm H2 and 0.050 M substrate at 0.100 mL/min, hydrogen is supplied at about 0.0446 mmol/min versus 0.00500 mmol/min substrate, or 8.92 molar equivalents of H2 per substrate throughput, assuming one H2 equivalent is required for hydrogenolysis.
pre_reactor_steps: Prepare a clear 0.050 M solution of N-diphenylmethylazetidin-3-ol in methanol; use the verified molecular weight of the actual substrate material when preparing the solution.
Do not add acetic acid in this first conservative screen, because acid availability and acid compatibility with the proposed packed bed are not confirmed by the authoritative inventory.

Charge the 5 mL packed-bed reactor with the Pd(OH)2/Al2O3 catalyst used in the batch precedent only if that catalyst is physically available and approved for fixed-bed hydrogen service. Record catalyst mass, packing method, and measured or estimated void volume.
Leak-test the assembled SS liquid path, mixer, reactor, BPR, and fittings using the site's approved hydrogen-service procedure before introducing substrate or heating.

Do not flush an air-containing system directly with hydrogen. Start only after the facility's approved oxygen-removal/commissioning procedure has been completed; an inert purge source or equivalent commissioning method is not included in the stated inventory and must be confirmed by the facility.
Set the BPR to 20 bar, establish 0.100 mL/min methanol/substrate flow and 1.0 sccm H2, then heat the packed bed to 60 C after stable pressure and flow are demonstrated.
post_reactor_steps: Maintain the 20 bar BPR downstream of the reactor during the run.
Route depressurized reactor effluent only to an approved hydrogen-safe, ventilated collection/vent handling arrangement under site procedure; do not vent hydrogen into an enclosed laboratory area.
Collect time-resolved liquid fractions after at least two nominal liquid reactor volumes (100 min) and assay substrate and 3-azetidinol product by an appropriate validated analytical method.

After the run, cool while maintaining controlled pressure, stop substrate feed, and follow the approved hydrogen shutdown/depressurization procedure. Do not assume that catalyst retained in the bed is inactive.
proposal.chemistry_notes: The intended transformation is hydrogenolytic removal of the N-diphenylmethyl substituent to give the 3-azetidinol product, using Pd(OH)2/Al2O3 and H2 as in the supplied batch precedent. The reported 38.1% batch yield indicates that conversion and/or selectivity are uncertain; the present conditions are therefore a first screen rather than a yield prediction. Methanol is retained as the batch solvent. Acetic acid is intentionally excluded from this first pass because it is optional in the batch text but is not confirmed as available inventory. Potential concerns to monitor include incomplete hydrogenolysis, adsorption or retention of amine/product on alumina, catalyst deactivation, and any competing hydrogenolysis or hydrogenation of the substrate.

stage_parameters.calculation_notes: The in-channel H2 flow uses Q_actual = Q_STP x (333.15/273.15) x (1.01325/21.013), treating the 20 bar BPR setting as barg. Combined-channel residence is 5.0 mL divided by 0.1000 + 0.0588 mL/min. Both residence values are nominal because true packed-bed void volume is unspecified.

reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: 60 C directly matches the supplied batch hydrogenation temperature and is below the 120 C reactor and 150 C tubing limits.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: 20 bar is within the mandated 10-20 bar range and uses an available 20 bar BPR. The higher allowed pressure is selected conservatively to improve hydrogen availability without exceeding certified hardware limits.
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: 0.100 mL/min is tenfold above the pump minimum of 0.010 mL/min, is readily controllable, and gives a 50 min nominal liquid residence time in the stated 5 mL reactor.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: 0.050 M is a deliberately modest initial concentration intended to reduce precipitation, viscosity, and heat-release concerns. Solubility must be confirmed experimentally before use.
reasoning_per_field.hydrogen_flow: 1.0 sccm is above the 0.1 sccm MFC minimum and well below its 100 sccm maximum. It provides approximately 8.9 molar equivalents of H2 relative to substrate feed while limiting gas holdup.
reasoning_per_field.residence_times: 50.0 min is the liquid-only nominal reactor-volume residence time. 31.5 min includes the estimated pressure-corrected H2 volumetric flow at 60 C and 20 barg. Neither substitutes for a measured bed-void residence time.
reasoning_per_field.materials: The specified SS packed-bed reactor and 1.0 mm SS tubing are hydrogen-service-compatible according to the inventory and remain within their stated pressure and temperature ratings.
reasoning_per_field.light_setup: No photochemical activation is indicated by the batch protocol and no light source is available.

proposal.literature_analogies: The direct experimental analogy is the supplied batch protocol: methanolic N-diphenylmethylazetidin-3-ol treated with H2 over Pd(OH)2/Al2O3 at 60 C for 5 h. This proposal preserves catalyst class, solvent, hydrogen reductant, and temperature while changing only the contacting mode to a fixed packed bed. No quantitative external flow precedent, catalyst loading, or selectivity claim is asserted.
safety_flags: Hydrogen is flammable; operate only with the certified H2 MFC and certified gas-liquid mixer listed, in an approved hydrogen-service ventilated enclosure with hydrogen detection and emergency shutoff under facility procedure.
Use the 20 bar BPR downstream of the reactor; confirm all reactor, tubing, fittings, and connections are rated to at least 20 bar at 60 C before pressurization.

Do not use direct H2 flushing of equipment that may contain air. The stated inventory does not identify an inert purge gas or evacuation equipment, so oxygen-free commissioning is a mandatory external facility-procedure confirmation before this screen starts.

Pd(OH)2/Al2O3 may be pyrophoric or retain adsorbed hydrogen when wet or dry; maintain it in an appropriate wetted/inert state and handle, unload, and dispose of it only under the catalyst supplier and facility safety procedures.
Methanol is flammable and toxic; use closed liquid handling and compatible waste collection.

Do not add the optional acetic acid in this first run; acid addition should be a separately reviewed follow-up variable after baseline conversion, catalyst stability, and corrosion compatibility are established.
Stop the run for pressure instability, loss of liquid flow, excessive pressure drop, evidence of bed plugging, leaks, or uncontrolled temperature behavior.

confidence.overall: moderate for equipment-compatible first-screen conditions; low for predicted conversion/yield
key_assumptions: Pd(OH)2/Al2O3 from the supplied batch protocol is available and can be safely packed in the listed reactor.
The substrate dissolves at 0.050 M in methanol at the feed and reactor temperatures.
The 5 mL reactor volume can be used as a nominal screening volume; actual catalyst-bed void volume will be measured or estimated before interpreting residence-time effects.
An approved oxygen-removal, H2 venting, detection, and emergency-shutdown procedure is available at the operating facility despite not being enumerated in the equipment inventory.
